properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-24 by Anthony: *"keep rocksdb 0.24 as-is. We can switch to rust-rocksdb in a future session that creates a PR for this switch."*

═══ WHAT HE SPOTTED, AND IT IS RIGHT ═══

There are TWO separate crates wrapping the same C++ engine, with independent version numbering:

    crate            declared      resolved            latest
    rocksdb          "0.24"        0.24.0              0.25.0     ← in use, historically unmaintained
    rust-rocksdb     --            --                  0.52.0     ← active, community-standard
    librocksdb-sys   --            0.17.3+10.4.2       --
    tantivy          --            0.26.1              --

reflow2 uses `rocksdb`, pinned at `dynograph-foundation/Cargo.toml:60`, one minor behind its own latest and on the less-maintained of the two. `rust-rocksdb` tracks current stable C++ RocksDB releases and carries the fuller feature set (transactions, backups, column families).

⚠️ **THE TWO VERSION NUMBERS ARE NOT COMPARABLE.** 0.24 vs 0.52 is not "28 versions behind" — they are different crates that never shared a numbering line. Reading them as one series would overstate the gap.

═══ WHY THIS BECOMES REFLOW2'S DECISION NOW ═══

Increment 4 of `dec:absorb-the-foundation-subset-and-end-the-dependency` absorbs `dynograph-storage`, which means reflow2 declares this dependency in its OWN manifest for the first time. "Which rocksdb crate, at which version" stops being dynograph's call and becomes reflow2's, on that branch, that day.

═══ WHAT WAS DECIDED, AND THE REASONING ═══

**Absorb `rocksdb = "0.24"` verbatim.** The migration stays purely mechanical: the same crate, the same version, the same API, so nothing about the 86-file absorption can fail for a reason other than the absorption.

**Then switch to `rust-rocksdb` in a separate PR**, with its own test run and its own revert.

⭐ THIS IS THE SAME PRINCIPLE THAT SPLIT THE ABSORPTION INTO INCREMENTS: one variable at a time, so a failure has one cause. Bumping even to `rocksdb` 0.25 inside this increment would mean a breakage had two candidate explanations, and the increment is already the largest by a wide margin — ~5,516 lines across ~86 files, bringing rocksdb and tantivy into the manifest together.

🛑 AND THE COST OF THE ALTERNATIVE IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL HERE. This project has already paid for attributing one effect to the wrong cause today: a 40-second regression was blamed on the wrong code because two numbers happened to agree. Mixing a dependency swap into a migration is the same shape, set up in advance.

═══ ROADS NOT TAKEN ═══
• **Bump to `rocksdb` 0.25 during the absorption** — smallest possible change, same crate. Declined for the two-causes reason; it buys one minor version at the price of an ambiguous failure.
• **Switch to `rust-rocksdb` 0.52 during the absorption** — the maintained crate, but an API change stacked on top of the largest migration in the plan.

📌 STILL PARKED, and deliberately: `dec:idea-a-byte-backend-that-compiles-in-seconds` (redb, fjall, LMDB, SQLite). Anthony, same exchange: *"I know we brainstormed switching to redb, but I'm still not convinced that is the right move - so that one stays parked for a time."* **Parked is not rejected**, and the spike he asked for stays owed. Note the ordering that makes it possible at all: the `KvBackend` trait is `pub(crate)` inside dynograph-storage, so no spike can be written from reflow2 until increment 4 lands.
properties.name: DECIDED — absorb the `rocksdb` 0.24 pin exactly as it is, and switch to the maintained `rust-rocksdb` in its own later PR
properties.rationale:
Recorded because the decision is small and the reasoning is the whole of it: absorbing verbatim is not laziness, it is keeping the number of variables at one.

⭐ THE FINDING IS ANTHONY'S AND IT WAS NOT VISIBLE FROM INSIDE THE PLAN. The absorption scoping measured lines, files, closures and type boundaries — and never asked whether the external crate being inherited was the right one. **A migration that faithfully carries a dependency forward will faithfully carry a bad choice of dependency forward too**, and nothing in the costing would have said so.
